panels.html:
Selena Review

Pros

  • Only character capable of replenishing enemy Tenacity Bars, giving her a unique niche in the meta

  • With the right build, she attacks through her allies via Coordinated Attacks and Mark and doesn’t need to do so herself.

  • Has many different build paths and unique Epiphanies, allowing for many Potential builds now and in the future

  • Can be played as a Ravage support, a Passion support or a main Damage Dealer, even though some are stronger than others depending on the current meta.

  • Has options to be able to deal high direct Tenacity Damage and apply Passion Weakness.

  • Capable single-target Potential with some solid AoE options if chosen via Epiphanies.

Cons

  • Primary meta build requires specific Epiphanies and isn’t functional based on base cards.

  • Most popular builds rely on allies to attack and use their cards for her to function in the team.

Review

Introduction

Selena is a 4-Star Passion attribute Ranger who best provides her damage from the sidelines in the form of Extra/Co-ordinated attacks. 

Selena's Damage mostly comes from ally Targeting Attack Cards, with her triggering a variety of Extra Attacks through her various effects on their Activation. Notably, she can trigger separate Extra Attacks off different conditions mainly off of High-Power Scope and Drone Bombing's Epiphanies. Selena is also capable of buffing Mark considerably with her Signature card, alongside her E6 allowing her to potentially multiply the efficiency of Marks activated by her.

Selena lacks any natural Card Draw in her kit; ideally, you'll want to pair her with other units who can offer Card Draw to alleviate this weakness. Selena also benefits greatly from additive buffs such as Morale due to relatively low damage on her Extra/Co-ordinated attacks to further boost her Potential damage output if you do plan on utilizing her Mark playstyle.

Review

Key Mechanics

  • Mark: Mark is a stackable debuff that Selena can apply through a wide variety of her cards, forming the core of her kit. When an enemy is marked and an Attack Card is used, Selena will fire an additional attack toward the marked target/s, dealing 100% ATK damage. To take advantage of this, Mark generation needs to be combined with high-frequency attacks to achieve the best results.

  • Break/Ravage: The other mechanic core to Selena’s identity is Break/Ravage and Tenacity Damage. Many of Selena’s abilities cause her attacks and additional attacks to either inflict additional Tenacity Damage or increase the Tenacity Damage dealt by a %. Building on this, Selena also has abilities that provide additional benefit each time an enemy is broken, further incentivizing a high Tenacity Damage break playstyle.

  • Attunement: Triggers listed “Attunement” effect when drawn naturally or via card effect. Does not activate if the card is “Moved” to the hand.

  • Passion Weakness: A debuff that causes the enemy to be treated as though they are Passion Weak for all Combatant attacks while it remains active. It is duration-based, not hit-count-based.

A deck most notably known for its synergy with Sereniel, but it can be used alongside any carry who may want to Ravage multiple times, like some Mei Lin builds. It utilizes Tactical Maneuver IV to refund an enemy’s tenacity, in order to ravage them multiple times, as is the case for her Sereniel team, where you get back your Homing Lasers (and create some) for every Ravage done. Additionally, she can add up to 2 extra attacks for every attack played, making her do a rather large amount of the team’s damage. Oftentimes more than the main ‘carry’ like Sereniel when played in an optimized set-up.

Deck utilizes Selena’s 3 different coordinates and ability to apply passion-weakness imprint to give Passion DPS +3-hits for every 1-hit she does, combined with her Mark buffs and certain interactions she can give up to +5 hits for every 1-attack a Passion DPS plays, making her incredibly strong with most Passion DPS who can play low-cost attacks frequently (Diana & Heidemarie being prime examples).
Synergies

Selena Synergies

Sereniel
  • Selena can enable a boss to be Ravaged up to 4 more times, which means the number of homing lasers Sereniel can effectively be multiplied by 3x (6 versus 2).
  • Selena can add up to 2 extra attacks on every Sereniel hit if her coordinated attack skills are played before Sereniel’s attacks. Meaning, you can potentially triple the amount of attacks you’re getting for every attack Sereniel plays.
  • Sereniel’s cards generally being start of hand makes Selena’s Potential draw issues less of a factor, further increasing their synergy.
Cassius
  • Through neutral morale Epiphanies on cards like Devil Dice or Dice Trick, Cass is able to give high additive buffing with little cost.
  • With Divine AP on Sereniel, she can circumvent the major hurdle of Cass, which is the cost of playing his cards or setting up initially and allow him to buff even more as he isn’t reliant on Divines himself.
  • Note: It can be challenging for many players to use Cassius effectively without Divine Epiphanies on him or Sereniel.
  • Cassius, being Instinct, means he benefits from Sereniel’s Plasma Missile Instinct Weakness Imprint alongside Selena’s Extra Attacks on Weakness Attack, giving him amazing synergy in assisting Ravages and facilitating more Extra Attacks.
  • He can net a decent amount of draw to ease the burden that Selena’s lack of draw might impose.
Rei
  • Without Divine Epiphanies, she has access to decent Morale buffs (most notably neutral Epiphany Morale on Snack-Time for a permanent 1 Morale per Snack-Time), which Sereniel and Selena can utilize well.
  • Oftentimes not the preferred option, but it is an easy one to make work in lower-end or lower-investment builds.
Heidemarie
  • Heidemarie is able to trigger all 3 of Selena’s coordinated attacks, alongside her having a way to trigger it a minimum of 20 times a turn with Sword Rain III duped 4x. This means they will do a minimum of 80-hits a turn played right.
  • Heidemarie benefits greatly from Selena’s ability to apply passion-weakness imprint as Heidemarie is one of the few extra attackers who benefits from it.

Investment

Selena Potential Priority

Selena’s Signature Potentials offer significant damage boosts as well as some additional functionality, making them a high priority to unlock.

  • 3-1: Causes Engagement Fire to deal Piercing Damage, which ignores enemy shields.

  • 5-1: Increases Engagement Fire’s damage multiplier by +5% with an additional +5% bonus granted if Bonus Additional Damage exceeds 15%.

  • 7: Increases Passion DMG% by +4% passively, with a further +4% increase unlocked if Bonus Additional Damage exceeds 30%.

Seasonal

Selena Seasonal Powers

Introduces Desire Cards. Desire Cards are cards that primarily exist to give a strong passive buff from meeting certain Desire Thresholds (3/5/7) which can only be done by having multiple ally decks also made in Season-4. 

  • For Desire Threshold, it’s common to run 1 Claim / 1 Survival / 1 Inquiry for use in a variety of builds; however, it's also common to just do 3 ‘X’ to meet effect easier or do 2 'X' / 1 Inquiry (to keep Sample Collection as Card Effect). This is extremely dependent on ally desire cards and individual team building goal.

’X’ refers to a ‘Placeholder for Specific Desire Threshold Goal’, i.e. if you are building your team for 7 Claim then you might do 2 Claim / 1 Inquiry.

Introduces Persona Cards and Engravings. Persona Cards are powerful cards that introduce new playstyles or ways of buffing/debuffing. Engravings are effects that can be applied to both the Persona Cards and Equipment, functioning near identically to Refinements of Season-2 but with new effects.

  • The most common Card Engraving to take for Attack Persona Cards is [For each Lux Engraving, 1 Mark to random enemies ] or [Attunement: Decrease Cost by 1 until used].

    • For Skill Persona Cards [When this card is Discarded, activate this card] is the recommended choice, provided you are playing this unit with a way to facilitate its discard. 

  • The most common Equipment Engraving to optimize for is [When 5 or more cards have been created through abilities by allies, +30% Damage Amount to Extra Attacks of this unit (1 time per turn)]. This effect stacks. But, other damage increase effects are viable just significantly worse for Extra Attack units than the dedicated Engraving.

Introduces Refinements, effects on Equipment that allow one to get additional Equipment effects for no Faint-Cost (post-S2), and God’s Hammer, a powerful effect that gives a random copy of any other Equipment effect on-top of current Equipment but costs 10 Faint Memory and is only gained from the Boss.

  • Increase Damage Amount of Extra Attacks by 25%.

Because God’s Hammer is completely RNG at the end of the run, we do not have a specific recommendation since the player has very little control over the decision but for ATK-based Attackers usually ATK% gear is considered best and DEF-based Attackers DEF% gear is considered best.

Introduces Forbidden Cards, powerful cards that create new synergies and can only be acquired once per run (can be duped at one event or via save data editing). 

  • Forbidden: Gesture of Freedom. Permanent Cost-Reduction to  one card, can be manipulated.

  • Forbidden: Portrait of Fury. ++Draw, +Damage

  • Forbidden: Ecstasy of Violence. +Damage

  • Forbidden: Eternal Hunger. +Draw, ++AP (Ally Reliant)

High-Power Scope I: Now applies 4 Mark (instead of 2) if the enemy is doing an attack action. This is one of the best ways of applying Mark quickly in a Mark-based Selena build, but Mark-based builds tend to be outperformed by Extra Attack or Supportive Selena builds, so it is not recommended.

High-Power Scope II: An Upgrade that has the effect of when Selena is using an Attack Card, apply 1 Mark to the enemy. This is one of the best Epiphanies for Selena Carry, but it's not recommended to use Selena Carry over her more Supportive / Sub-DPS alternatives that often offer higher damage and need less work, to work.

High-Power Scope III: 50% additive buff to Mark. This is a nice additional buff to Mark-based builds, but Mark-based builds tend to be outperformed by Extra Attack or Supportive Selena builds, so it is not recommended. Moreover, the extremely specific and conditional buff to Mark is worse than just generic buffs

High-Power Scope IV: Does an Extra Attack when an ally uses an Attack Card. This is her go-to Epiphany, essentially an unconditional Extra Attack after being played–do note that duping/playing multiple only increases the duration of the effect, not the damage.

High-Power Scope V: An Upgrade that applies 1 Mark to enemies at start of turn. Moreover, it’s an Upgrade that can activate Quantum Collector’s damage boost on Upgrade for OTK-setups that Selena is sometimes used in.

Neutral: Target Neutral Epiphany: Draw 1.
With Draw 1, it is easier to keep it as it doesn’t put strain on your draw needs for its relatively low value; however, it still has the issue of it being a much worse value than High-Power Scope IV in terms of damage and often needing to be duped for value.

Target Spotted I: Does a small attack when Attunement is activated, loses the Mark effect. This can be used like a pseudo-Extra Attack with Precision Aim or Nia’s Adagio (to re-activate the Attunement effect), but it doesn’t benefit from Extra Attack% like Selena’s normal Extra Attacks would (and takes a ton of steps to utilize), so it is not recommended to build around.

Target Spotted II: An attack that applies 4 Mark if enemy is in a Mark state. This is one of the best ways of applying Mark quickly in a Mark-based Selena build, but Mark-based builds tend to be outperformed by Extra Attack or Supportive Selena builds so it is not recommended.

Target Spotted III: Now, a Skill that shields and applies the 2 Mark to all enemies. Can be a decent card for auto-farming AOE simulations, but it isn’t an especially strong effect in any difficult content and not recommended to take.

Target Spotted IV: Changes to a Skill that shields and loses its Mark but gains ‘Attunement: Draw 1’. This has good synergy with effects like Precision Aim and Nia’s Adagio Epiphanies, as it will allow the card to be used as a draw engine; however, oftentimes it's easier to just build thin decks or have Divines on other options rather than optimize in this way.

Target Spotted V: Now, an Upgrade that does a strong Extra Attack on Ravage. This is the go-to choice in most builds that is worth keeping, since it presents no strain on your deck after Turn 1 and is effectively free damage. Moreover, it’s an Upgrade that can activate Quantum Collector’s damage boost on Upgrade for OTK-setups that Selena is sometimes used in.

Neutral: Target Neutral Epiphany: Draw 1.
Draw 1 basically just makes it so the card can be worth keeping and slightly worse value than Target Spotted V in most teams.

Drone Bombing I: Now is 2 Passion Weakness Imprint. This practically guarantees 100% uptime on it, making it a noticeable Upgrade over the base card. The only reason this isn’t rated higher is because there are many other ways to get Passion Weakness Imprint, specifically, from other avenues (Lucas, Mei Lin etc.) which makes it less of a strong use-case for Selena specifically.

Drone Bombing II: Loses Passion Weakness, but gains 2 Mark effect when Passion card is played before it. The damage of options like IV and V being vastly superior makes this not a recommended choice for damage, and the utility of options like Neutral or Drone I being much stronger makes it not recommended as a utility option.

Drone Bombing III: A weak AOE attack that gets significantly stronger for every Passion Attack Card played. Because it is only a Passion Attack Card and not Passion cards, in general, it is significantly harder to get value out of this compared to Mei Lin’s effects, which are ALL Passion cards (has very little synergy with Veronica for example).

Drone Bombing IV: Effect is now: Extra Attack when ally attacks Weakness (has Elemental Advantage on attack). This, in combination with High-Power Scope IV, allows Selena to do 2 Extra Attacks for every attack an ally does, provided the ally has Weakness Imprint / Elemental Advantage, which allies like Sereniel and Mei Lin should always have.

Drone Bombing V: Now, an Upgrade that allows Selena to do an Extra Attack for every Passion card played. This is an incredibly strong card when used alongside a Passion DPS, like Mei Lin (or Selena carry), who attacks a lot. However, it has very little value when not used with a Passion DPS.

Neutral: Target Neutral Epiphany: Draw 1.
Draw 1 can make it much easier to keep this card for the Weakness Imprint (Elemental Advantage), which is an incredibly strong effect on characters that can use it. The only reason this isn’t rated higher is because there are many other ways to get Passion Weakness Imprint, specifically, from other avenues (Lucas, Mei Lin etc.), which makes it less of a strong use-case for Selena specifically.

Tactical Maneuver I: Now a bit more shield and 3 Tenacity Damage instead of 2. Much like the base Epiphany, Tenacity Damage isn’t particularly high value in the current balance and is probably not worth keeping in your deck.

Tactical Maneuver II: Now a decent attack that does extra Tenacity Damage. Selena’s damage generally comes from Extra Attacks, which this can facilitate in a Selena Carry deck; however, Selena Carry isn’t a popular use nor is it recommended.

Tactical Maneuver III: Gains an additional effect of 2 Mark if the target is already Ravaged. Can be useful in a Mark-based Selena build, but this is not her most popular nor recommended use-case.

Tactical Maneuver IV: Becomes a 0-cost card with the effect of restoring the Tenacity Bar of the target to full. This is the go-to Epiphany, with Selena’s main utility feature that sets her apart from all other Support/Sub-DPS. If not playing this Epiphany (like for Extra Attacker build), the card is typically just removed.

Tactical Maneuver V: Now hits all enemies but is only 1 Tenacity Damage and 1 Mark. Can be a decent card for auto-farming AOE simulations, but it isn’t an especially strong effect in any difficult content and not recommended to take.
